newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine miners saddled with bikes for cash.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine miners saddled with bikes for cash.

text.p: Ukraine's government on Tuesday came up with a new solution to clear a huge backlog in miners' wages -- pay them off with motorcycles.
A government order asked the Kiev Motorcycle Plant to make the bikes available "with the aim of settling the wage debt to workers in the coal sector".
The firm manufactures heavy motorcycles with sidecars. They remain largely unpopular with the few Ukrainian consumers wealthy enough to afford one.

Miners, who last went on strike in July to press demands for backpay, are among hundreds of thousands of workers, also including teachers and doctors, who have gone unpaid for months, The wage backlog totals the equivalent of about $1.7 billion.
Ministers say the government can provide no more money to the miners and blame the shortfall on the failure of industry to pay promptly, if at all, for coal supplies.
Anecdotal evidence shows that the practice of paying workers in goods rather than hard cash is still common five years after independence from Soviet rule.
The weekly Zerkalo Nedeli reported that miners had been receiving potatoes from collective farmers unable otherwise to pay for heating coal.
Sugar refineries pay workers in sacks of sugar. Factories in the provinces regularly distribute unsold production to workers who then travel to Kiev to sell them on open markets.
